newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mark strengthens on French election by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Mark strengthens on French election by late Tokyo.

text.p: The mark had strengthened against major currencies by late Tokyo on Monday in reaction to an unexpected lead by left-wing opposition parties in the first round of French parliamentary elections on Sunday.
The surprising turn in France increased doubts about a smooth passage towards European economic and monetary union (EMU) and supported the German currency, dealers said.

The opposition Socialists, Communists, extreme-left and other left-wing candidates took the lead over the ruling coalition and other moderate-right candidates in Sunday's first round vote in the election for the 577-seat National Assembly.

The mark, seen as a stronger currency on its own amid political uncertainty in France, was bought across the board, dragging the dollar/mark rate down as low as 1.6778 marks, compared with 1.6931/36 marks at Friday's New York close.
It also received a boost against the yen, standing at 68.86/89 yen at 0646 GMT against 68.25 yen in late New York on Friday.
"The surprising outcome encouraged traders to cover their short-positions in the mark against the yen in Tokyo," a dealer at French bank said.

In addition to doubts over the Socialists' stance on EMU, a rise in votes won by Communists and the extreme right, who are not eager to meet the tough fiscal goals for joining EMU, pushed the French franc down against the mark. "Uncertainty remains as we don't know how much those extreme opinions by those parties will affect the next government," said Hidemitsu Terry Terasawa, manager of the foreign exchange and treasury division at the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Mark/French franc stood around 3.3755/60 at 0700 GMT, compared with 3.3695/00 in late Friday in Europe.
But trade became thin as trading energy ebbed in the afternoon amid a lack of fresh factors and ahead of market holidays in London and New York, dealers said.

In mark/yen trade, exporter offers were expected above 69 yen, capping the mark's further gains, while Japanese exporters were thought to be keen to sell dollars above 116.30 yen in order to arrange the conversion of their overseas earnings into yen in the future, dealers said. Dollar/yen was stuck in a narrow range just below 116 yen for most of afternoon trade.
"It seems like the 115 yen level is a comfortable level for monetary officials and we don't hear many remarks on currencies from them (today)," said a long-term credit bank dealer.

A dealer at a European bank in Singapore said fears that EMU might be delayed on talk that most of the members would be unable to meet the criteria was also causing mark purchases for its safe haven status. But some dealers in Tokyo said a left-wing parties' victory in the second ballot of the French election on June 1 might be a minus factor for the EMU and could eventually prompt dollar buying for marks. --- Singapore newsroom +65-8703080, Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8584
